00-about > About Meridian Dental & Aesthetics

# About Meridian Dental & Aesthetics
Meridian Dental & Aesthetics is a private dental and facial aesthetics group with three
London locations: Docklands, Shoreditch and Clapham. The group has been operating since
2014 and sees around 400 patients a week across the three sites.

## What kind of practice this is
Fully private, general dentistry led, with a facial aesthetics service that grew out of
patient demand rather than being bolted on. There is no NHS contract at any site.

The practice is not a chain and is not corporate owned. Decisions about how long an
appointment runs are made by the clinician rather than by a booking target, which is why
appointment lengths here are longer than average and why the fees are what they are.

## Ownership and clinical governance
Meridian is a partnership between two principal dentists. Clinical governance is overseen by
a lead clinician at each site, and the group holds a monthly clinical governance meeting
covering audit, incidents and complaints.

All clinicians are registered with the General Dental Council. The aesthetics team are
registered nurses working under a prescriber, and the lead aesthetics practitioner is an
independent prescriber in her own right.

## Which site does what
Docklands is the largest site and the group's main location, with six surgeries. It offers
general dentistry, hygiene with a dedicated hygienist, the full facial aesthetics list, and
the group's only panoramic X-ray machine.

Shoreditch has three surgeries and offers general dentistry and hygiene. It does not offer
aesthetics.

Clapham has three surgeries and offers general dentistry and facial aesthetics. It does not
have a dedicated hygiene chair, so hygiene appointments at Clapham run through a general
surgery and take 40 minutes rather than 30.

It does not have a dedicated hygiene chair, so hygiene appointments at Clapham run through a general surgery and take 40 minutes rather than 30.

## How the practice runs
Appointments are longer than the industry average by design. A routine examination is 20
minutes where 10 is common, and a new patient examination is 40.

Treatment is planned in writing before it is booked. Nobody is asked to agree to a cost in
the chair, and the treatment coordinators exist so that a long plan is discussed properly
rather than at the front desk with a queue behind you.

## Languages
Front desk and clinical staff between them speak English, Portuguese, Bengali, Polish and
Cantonese. If a patient needs a specific language, the front desk can arrange for a
colleague who speaks it to be present at the appointment, or book a professional interpreter
with a week's notice at no charge.

## Contact
General enquiries and booking for all three sites go through the Docklands front desk on
020 7946 0812, Monday to Friday 8am to 6pm and Saturday 9am to 2pm. Outside those hours the
answerphone gives the NHS 111 number for urgent problems.

01-services > Services

# Services


## General dentistry
Routine examinations, fillings, extractions, crowns, bridges, veneers, inlays, onlays and
root canal treatment.

A routine examination takes 20 minutes. It covers a check of every tooth, a soft tissue
examination of the cheeks, tongue and floor of the mouth, a basic periodontal examination
score, and small bitewing X-rays where clinically indicated. Bitewings are usually taken
every two years for a low-risk patient and annually for someone with a history of decay.

A new patient examination takes 40 minutes. It adds a full charting of existing
restorations, a six-point periodontal chart if the basic screening flags anything, a jaw
joint check, and a written treatment plan emailed afterwards. The plan lists each item, the
band it falls in, and the order things should be done in.

Fillings are white composite as standard. Amalgam is no longer placed at any Meridian site.
A composite filling takes 30 to 45 minutes depending on how many surfaces are involved.

Root canal treatment on a front tooth is usually one appointment of 60 to 75 minutes. A
molar is usually two appointments of 90 minutes, two to three weeks apart, with a temporary
dressing in between. A molar root canal is followed by a crown in most cases, because the
remaining tooth structure is brittle.

Crowns and veneers are made by a laboratory in Kent and take two weeks. You leave the first
appointment with a temporary and come back for the fit, which takes 30 minutes.

01-services > Services > General dentistry

molar root canal is followed by a crown in most cases, because the remaining tooth structure is brittle. Crowns and veneers are made by a laboratory in Kent and take two weeks. You leave the first appointment with a temporary and come back for the fit, which takes 30 minutes.

## Hygiene
Scale and polish, air-flow stain removal, and periodontal maintenance.

A standard hygiene appointment is 30 minutes and covers ultrasonic scaling above and just
below the gum line, hand scaling where needed, and a polish. Air-flow adds 15 minutes and
uses a pressurised powder spray that lifts staining from tea, coffee, red wine and smoking
more effectively than a polish alone.

Deep cleaning, properly called root surface debridement, is carried out under local
anaesthetic and split across two appointments of 45 minutes, one per side of the mouth,
usually two weeks apart. It is followed by a review at eight to twelve weeks to re-chart
the pockets and see what has responded.

Periodontal maintenance for a patient with treated gum disease runs at three or four month
intervals rather than six, and each appointment is 40 minutes.

Hygiene is available at Docklands and Shoreditch with a dedicated hygienist. Clapham runs
hygiene through a general surgery, so those appointments are 40 minutes rather than 30.

01-services > Services > Hygiene

for a patient with treated gum disease runs at three or four month intervals rather than six, and each appointment is 40 minutes. Hygiene is available at Docklands and Shoreditch with a dedicated hygienist. Clapham runs hygiene through a general surgery, so those appointments are 40 minutes rather than 30.

## Facial aesthetics
Anti-wrinkle injections, dermal filler, skin boosters, chemical peels, and medical-grade
skincare consultations.

Every aesthetics patient has a consultation before any treatment. The consultation is 30
minutes, covers medical history, what you want to change, what is realistic, and the risks.
There is a mandatory two-week cooling-off period between a first consultation and a
first-time dermal filler treatment. Anti-wrinkle treatment can be carried out on the same
day as the consultation for a returning patient, but not for a first-time patient, who is
booked back after 48 hours.

Anti-wrinkle treatment takes 20 minutes and is reviewed at two weeks. The two-week review
is free and is when any adjustment is done.

Dermal filler appointments are 45 minutes for one area and 60 for two. Filler is
hyaluronic acid based and is reversible with hyaluronidase if there is a problem.

Skin boosters are a course of three, four weeks apart, each 30 minutes.

Chemical peels are 45 minutes. A course of four is usual for pigmentation, and peels are
not carried out on skin that has had recent sun exposure.

Aesthetics is available at Docklands and Clapham. Shoreditch does not offer aesthetics.

01-services > Services > Facial aesthetics

are a course of three, four weeks apart, each 30 minutes. Chemical peels are 45 minutes. A course of four is usual for pigmentation, and peels are not carried out on skin that has had recent sun exposure. Aesthetics is available at Docklands and Clapham. Shoreditch does not offer aesthetics.

## Whitening
Take-home whitening with custom trays, and in-surgery whitening.

Take-home requires two appointments. The first, 30 minutes, takes impressions or a digital
scan. The second, 20 minutes, fits the trays and hands over the gel with instructions. The
gel is worn for two to four hours a day, or overnight for the lower-strength option, over
two to three weeks.

In-surgery whitening is a single appointment of 90 minutes and gets to a similar end point
in one visit, with more short-term sensitivity. Most patients who have in-surgery whitening
also take home trays for maintenance.

Whitening requires a dental examination within the previous six months. It cannot be
carried out on patients with active decay, untreated gum disease, or during pregnancy or
breastfeeding. It does not change the colour of crowns, veneers or white fillings, so
existing restorations at the front of the mouth may need replacing afterwards to match.

## Emergency appointments
Each site holds two emergency slots per weekday, released at 8am on the day. Emergency
appointments are 20 minutes and are for pain, swelling, trauma, or a lost filling or crown.

They are assessment appointments. The clinician will get you comfortable, which often means
dressing a tooth or draining a swelling, and book the definitive treatment separately.

Out of hours there is no on-call service. The answerphone gives the NHS 111 number, which
is the correct route for severe pain or facial swelling overnight or on a Sunday.

## Extras
X-rays are £25 each and are included in the new patient examination fee where clinically

There is no charge for a treatment plan, no charge for the two-week anti-wrinkle review,

## What moves a quote within its band
Where the tooth is, how much of it is left, whether the work is being redone, and how long
the appointment needs to be. A crown on a heavily broken-down molar that needs a build-up
first sits at the top of the band. A straightforward crown on a well-prepared premolar sits
at the bottom.

The clinician gives you the specific figure at the examination, in writing, before anything
is booked.

03-appointment-prep > Preparing for your appointment

# Preparing for your appointment


## What to bring
Bring a list of any medication you take, including anything bought over the counter and any
supplements, because several of them affect bleeding and healing. Bring the name and
address of your previous dentist if you have had treatment in the last two years.

If you have had X-rays elsewhere in the last twelve months, ask that practice to email them
across and we can often avoid repeating them. Ours is a referrals address on the website and
the front desk will give it to you.

Bring your reading glasses if you use them. The consent forms and the treatment plan are
easier that way.

## Arriving
Arrive five minutes early for a routine appointment and fifteen minutes early for a first
visit, because the medical history form takes a few minutes. The form can also be completed
online from the link in the confirmation email, which is faster and means you can arrive
five minutes before instead.

The confirmation email goes out when you book and a text reminder goes out 48 hours before.
If neither arrived, check the address and number we hold, because that is usually what has
gone wrong.

## Before hygiene
Eat beforehand if you can, because the mouth is uncomfortable for a while afterwards and
because a scale and polish on an empty stomach is a longer 30 minutes than it needs to be.

Brush normally. There is no need to do anything special, and scrubbing hard beforehand
makes the gums bleed more during the appointment.

Avoid staining food and drink for 24 hours afterwards, so no red wine, coffee, tea, curry or
berries.

chunks.headingPath: Preparing for your appointment > Before hygiene
chunks.content:
03-appointment-prep > Preparing for your appointment > Before hygiene

is a longer 30 minutes than it needs to be. Brush normally. There is no need to do anything special, and scrubbing hard beforehand makes the gums bleed more during the appointment. Avoid staining food and drink for 24 hours afterwards, so no red wine, coffee, tea, curry or berries.

## Before whitening
Have a scale and polish within the two weeks before whitening starts. Whitening works on
clean enamel and the result is noticeably more even.

Use a sensitive toothpaste for two weeks beforehand if you know your teeth are sensitive. It
makes a real difference to how comfortable the first few days are.

Do not book whitening in the two weeks before a wedding or similar. Sensitivity and small
patchy areas settle in the first fortnight and you want to be past that.

## Before facial aesthetics
Avoid alcohol for 24 hours beforehand. Avoid ibuprofen, aspirin, fish oil, vitamin E and
ginkgo for 48 hours where it is safe for you to do so, because they all increase bruising.
Do not stop prescribed blood thinners without speaking to whoever prescribed them.

Do not book aesthetics within two weeks of a dental appointment involving local anaesthetic,
and do not book dental treatment within two weeks after filler.

Come without make-up if you can, or allow ten minutes to remove it at the clinic.

Do not book anything with visible downtime in the week before an event. Filler swelling
peaks at 48 hours and bruising can take a week.

## Before a child's appointment
Bring a parent or guardian who can consent. Under-16s cannot be seen without an adult with
parental responsibility present for the whole appointment. A grandparent or childminder
cannot consent unless they hold parental responsibility.

Book a morning slot if you can. Children handle dental appointments better before lunch, and
the front desk will say so if you ask.

## If you are unwell
If you have a fever, a chest infection, or anything contagious, call and move the
appointment. There is no charge for cancelling because you are ill, at any notice.

04-cancellation > Cancellation, changes and missed appointments

# Cancellation, changes and missed appointments


## Notice
We ask for 24 hours' notice to change or cancel an appointment. For appointments longer
than 45 minutes, which includes in-surgery whitening, deep cleaning and most aesthetics
treatment, we ask for 48 hours.

Notice can be given by phone, by replying to the reminder text, or by email. The reply to
the reminder text is the fastest and reaches the right site automatically.

## Charges
A first missed appointment carries no charge. A second missed appointment within twelve
months is charged at 50% of the appointment fee. A third means we ask for a deposit before
booking anything longer than 30 minutes.

Short-notice cancellation, meaning inside the notice period, is treated the same as a missed
appointment for counting purposes.

The charge is waived for illness, bereavement, a caring emergency, or anything else that
would obviously count. Tell the front desk what happened and it comes off. Nobody is asked
for evidence.

## Deposits
A deposit is taken for in-surgery whitening, deep cleaning, and any aesthetics appointment
booked at Docklands on a Saturday, because Saturday aesthetics slots are the ones that go
unfilled when someone does not turn up.

The deposit is £75 and comes off the final bill. It is refunded in full if the appointment
is changed with the required notice, and is kept if it is not.

## Running late
If you are more than ten minutes late for a 20-minute appointment we will usually need to
rebook, because the surgery runs to the next patient. For a 40-minute appointment there is
more room and it is often still workable at fifteen minutes late.

Call ahead. The front desk will tell you honestly whether it is worth continuing your
journey, and would rather do that than have you arrive to be turned away.

## If we cancel
If a clinician is off sick we call as early as we can and offer the next available slot with
them, or an earlier slot with a colleague. If the cancellation was ours and you had taken
time off work, say so, and the rebooked appointment is prioritised.

## Waiting list and short-notice list
If nothing suitable is open we can add you to the short-notice list. When someone cancels we
text the list in order and the first person to reply takes the slot. Most people on the list
get an offer within eight working days, and it is free to be on it.

Say which sites and which days work for you when you join the list, because a list entry
that only works one afternoon a week rarely gets matched.

05-locations > Locations, travel and parking

# Locations, travel and parking


## Docklands
Meridian Docklands, Unit 4, Marsh Wall, London E14 9SH. This is the group's main site and
the largest, with six surgeries.

Getting there: five minutes' walk from South Quay on the DLR, and twelve minutes from
Canary Wharf on the Jubilee line. The 277 and D3 bus routes stop on Marsh Wall.

Parking: six patient bays behind the building, accessed from the service road off Marsh
Wall. They are first come, first served and free for two hours with a code from reception,
which you enter on the keypad by the barrier. The surrounding streets are pay and display
Monday to Saturday, 8am to 6.30pm. Docklands is outside the Congestion Charge zone but
inside the ULEZ.

Access: step-free throughout, automatic front door, and an accessible WC on the ground
floor. There is a hearing loop at the front desk.

## Shoreditch
Meridian Shoreditch, 118 Curtain Road, London EC2A 3AH. Three surgeries.

Getting there: four minutes from Old Street on the Northern line and eight minutes from
Shoreditch High Street on the Overground.

Parking: no patient parking at this site. The nearest car park is the NCP multi-storey on
Great Eastern Street, roughly a four-minute walk. Shoreditch sits inside both the
Congestion Charge zone and the ULEZ, so driving here on a weekday is expensive and we
generally suggest the tube.

Access: the surgeries are on the first floor and there is a lift. The lift is large enough
for a wheelchair but not for a stretcher.

## Clapham
Meridian Clapham, 7 Voltaire Road, London SW4 6DH. Three surgeries.

Getting there: six minutes from Clapham High Street on the Overground and nine minutes from
Clapham Common on the Northern line. The 88 and 345 stop on Clapham Road.

Access: step-free at the front and all surgeries are on the ground floor.

## Opening hours
Docklands: Monday to Friday 8am to 6pm, Saturday 9am to 2pm.
Shoreditch: Monday to Friday 8.30am to 6pm, Saturday 9am to 2pm.

## Moving between sites
Your records are shared across all three sites, so you can be seen at whichever is
convenient without transferring anything. Your usual clinician does not move with you,
though, so if you want to stay with the same person you need to book at their site.

## What is at which site
Docklands has general dentistry, hygiene, the full aesthetics list, and the group's only
panoramic X-ray machine. Shoreditch has general dentistry and hygiene. Clapham has general
dentistry and aesthetics, with hygiene run through a general surgery.

06-payment > Payment, insurance and plans

# Payment, insurance and plans


## How to pay
Card, Apple Pay and Google Pay at all three sites. Payment is taken at the end of the
appointment, not in advance, except where a deposit applies.

Treatment over £600 can be split, with half taken on the day of the first appointment and
the balance on completion. There is no charge for splitting a payment this way.

We do not take cash at Shoreditch. Docklands and Clapham take cash up to £500 per
transaction. We cannot take bank transfers for treatment, and we do not take cheques.

A receipt is emailed automatically after every payment. Itemised receipts with treatment
codes are what most insurers need, and those are produced as standard.

## Insurance
Meridian is not a registered provider with any insurer, so we do not bill insurers
directly and we cannot check your cover for you. You pay us and claim back.

The itemised receipt carries the treatment codes your policy will ask for. Patients on
Bupa, AXA, Denplan and WPE policies routinely claim back against Meridian receipts. If your
insurer wants a pre-treatment estimate, ask at the examination and the treatment plan is
formatted to suit.

## Membership plan
The Meridian Plan is £24.50 a month. It covers two examinations and two hygiene
appointments in a twelve-month period, all routine X-rays, and a 15% discount on
restorative treatment and 10% on whitening and aesthetics.

The plan runs on a rolling monthly direct debit with a three-month minimum term. After
that you can cancel any time with one month's notice. It does not cover treatment already
recommended before you joined, and it does not cover emergency assessments, which are
charged at the usual rate.

There is a family version at £22 a month per person for three or more people at the same
address.

## Finance
Interest-free finance over six or twelve months is available on treatment plans over
£1,000, subject to a credit check by our finance partner. Longer terms up to 36 months are

The application is completed on a tablet at the practice and takes about ten minutes for a

Meridian is a fully private group. We do not hold an NHS contract and cannot see patients

time.

## Refunds
If a laboratory-made item fails within twelve months through no fault of the patient it is
remade at no charge. Refunds on completed treatment are considered case by case by the
practice manager and are not automatic.

08-aftercare > Aftercare

# Aftercare


## After a filling
If you had local anaesthetic, avoid eating until the numbness has gone, usually two to
three hours. The commonest injury after a filling is a bitten lip or cheek in a child who
ate too soon.

Sensitivity to cold for a few days is normal and settles. Sensitivity that lingers more than
two weeks, pain that wakes you at night, or pain on biting that is getting worse after a
week, is not normal and you should call us. It usually means the bite needs adjusting, which
takes five minutes, or that the nerve is unhappy, which needs a proper look.

A white filling is fully set before you leave, so you can eat on it as soon as the numbness
has gone.

## After an extraction
Do not rinse at all for 24 hours. Rinsing washes out the clot and a lost clot is what
causes a dry socket, which is the painful complication people remember.

After 24 hours, rinse gently with warm salty water four times a day for a week, a teaspoon
of salt in a mug of warm water.

No smoking for 72 hours, no alcohol for 24 hours, nothing hot to drink on the day, and no
strenuous exercise for 48 hours. Some oozing on the first evening is expected and looks
worse mixed with saliva than it is.

If bleeding restarts, roll the gauze into a firm pad, place it over the socket and bite
firmly for 30 minutes without checking it. If it is still bleeding heavily after an hour of
proper pressure, call the practice, or go to A&E if we are closed.

A dry socket typically starts three to four days afterwards as a deep ache that painkillers
barely touch, often with a bad taste. Call us. It is dressed in a ten-minute appointment and
the relief is immediate.

08-aftercare > Aftercare > After an extraction

proper pressure, call the practice, or go to A&E if we are closed. A dry socket typically starts three to four days afterwards as a deep ache that painkillers barely touch, often with a bad taste. Call us. It is dressed in a ten-minute appointment and the relief is immediate.

## After hygiene
Gums may be tender and may bleed a little for a day or two. Use a soft brush and keep
brushing, because stopping makes it worse and the bleeding settles within a week in almost
everyone.

Sensitivity at the necks of the teeth is common after a thorough clean, particularly the
first one after a long gap. Sensitive toothpaste rubbed on with a finger and left rather
than rinsed off works better than brushing with it.

Avoid staining food and drink for 24 hours.

## After deep cleaning
Expect the gums to be sore for two or three days and to shrink back a little over the next
few weeks, which can leave gaps between the teeth and more sensitivity. That is the
treatment working rather than a complication, but nobody enjoys it and it is better to know
in advance.

Interdental brushes are the single thing that determines whether deep cleaning holds. The
hygienist will size them for you.

## After whitening
Sensitivity for 24 to 48 hours is common and settles. Use the desensitising gel supplied,
in the trays, for 30 minutes at a time.

Stick to a white diet for the first 48 hours: no red wine, coffee, tea, curry, berries,
beetroot or tomato sauce. Smoking undoes whitening faster than anything on that list.

The shade lifts for about two weeks after you stop, so judge the result then rather than on
the last day of treatment.

## After anti-wrinkle injections
Stay upright for four hours. No exercise for 24 hours, no facials, saunas or steam rooms for
48 hours, and do not rub or massage the area.

Small raised bumps at the injection points settle within an hour. Pinpoint bruises are
common and cover easily.

The effect appears over three to seven days and is fully settled at two weeks, which is when
it is reviewed and adjusted if needed. Do not judge it at day three.

08-aftercare > Aftercare > After anti-wrinkle injections

Small raised bumps at the injection points settle within an hour. Pinpoint bruises are common and cover easily. The effect appears over three to seven days and is fully settled at two weeks, which is when it is reviewed and adjusted if needed. Do not judge it at day three.

## After dermal filler
Swelling is normal and peaks at about 48 hours. Small bruises are common and can take a
week to fade. Sleep on your back for two nights and avoid make-up over the area for 12
hours.

Avoid dental treatment for two weeks, and avoid facials, saunas and sunbeds for a fortnight.

Firm lumps that are still there at two weeks should be reviewed. Blanching, meaning skin
that goes white and stays white, severe pain out of proportion to the treatment, or any
change in vision, needs to be reported immediately, on the same day, by phone.

## When to call us rather than wait
Facial swelling that is spreading, difficulty swallowing or opening the mouth, a temperature
alongside dental pain, bleeding that has not stopped after an hour of pressure, or any
vision change after filler. Those are same-day calls.

09-new-patients > New patients

# New patients


## Registering
There is no registration fee and no waiting list to join. Book a new patient examination and
the registration is completed at that appointment. You do not need a referral and you do not
need to have been seen anywhere recently.

## The first appointment
Forty minutes. It covers a medical history, a full charting of the teeth and any existing
work, a periodontal screening, a soft tissue and jaw joint check, X-rays where clinically
indicated, and a conversation about what you actually want from your teeth.

You leave with a written treatment plan by email, usually the same day and always within
two working days. The plan lists each item with its band, and the order things should be
done in, so you can decide what to do and when.

Nothing is treated at the first appointment except an emergency. If something needs doing
urgently the clinician will say so and get you comfortable, and the rest is booked
separately.

## Transferring records
Ask your previous practice to email your records and recent X-rays to the referrals address
on the website. Most send them within a fortnight. You do not need to wait for them to be
booked in, and we will not delay your appointment for them.

If your previous practice charges for records, that is between you and them. Under UK data
protection rules they cannot charge for a first copy in most circumstances.

## Nervous patients
Tell the front desk when you book and the appointment goes with a clinician who runs longer
slots, usually Dr Okafor at Docklands.

You can come in first just to see the room and meet the dentist with nothing done at all.
That is a familiarisation visit, it takes fifteen minutes, and there is no charge. People
use it more than you would think and nobody finds it odd.

Say what specifically you find difficult, because the answers are different. Needles, the
drill sound, gagging, and not being able to stop are four different problems with four
different approaches.

## Children
Under-16s must be accompanied by an adult with parental responsibility for the whole
appointment. A child examination is £45.

First visits for small children are deliberately short and often amount to a ride in the
chair and a count of the teeth. That is the intention, not a wasted appointment.

## What we need from you when you book
A name, a contact number, an email address for the confirmation and the plan, and a rough
sense of what the appointment is for. That is all. We do not ask for card details to hold a
routine appointment.

## Referrals from other practices
We accept referrals by email to the referrals address on the website. A referred patient is
contacted within three working days. Endodontic referrals go to Dr Rana at Docklands.

10-faq > Common questions

# Common questions


## How soon can I be seen?
Routine examinations are usually available within a week at Docklands and Clapham, and
within two weeks at Shoreditch. New patient examinations run about two weeks across all
three sites. Emergency slots are released at 8am each weekday, two per site.

## Do I need an examination before hygiene?
Yes if you are new to us, or if your last examination with us was more than twelve months
ago. Existing patients seen within twelve months can book hygiene directly.

This is not an upsell. A hygienist cannot safely clean around a tooth nobody has looked at,
and undiagnosed decay under the gum line is exactly what a clean will not fix.

## Can I see a specific clinician?
Yes. Say who when you book. It can add a week or so to the wait depending on their list, and
more for a new patient appointment with Dr Rana.

## Do you do house calls or online consultations?
No home visits at all. Aesthetics consultations can be done by video first, but any
treatment requires an in-person assessment on a separate day. Dental problems cannot be
assessed by video and we will not try.

## What if I am pregnant?
Tell us when you book. Routine examinations and hygiene are safe throughout pregnancy and
the second trimester is the most comfortable time for anything longer.

Elective X-rays and whitening are deferred until after the birth. Facial aesthetics is not
carried out during pregnancy or while breastfeeding.

## Do you treat anxious patients?
Yes, and it is a large part of what Dr Okafor does. Ask for a longer appointment when you
book, and consider a familiarisation visit first, which is free.

## Can I bring someone with me?
Yes, one person. For aesthetics consultations we actively encourage it, because a second
opinion in the room tends to produce more realistic decisions.

chunks.headingPath: Common questions > Do you have parking?
chunks.content:
10-faq > Common questions > Do you have parking?

## Do you have parking?
Docklands has six patient bays behind the building, free for two hours with a code from
reception. Shoreditch has none and the nearest is the Great Eastern Street multi-storey.

## Is there anywhere to leave a bike?
There are two Sheffield stands directly outside Docklands and a rack in the yard at
Shoreditch. Clapham has on-street stands about thirty metres along Voltaire Road.

## How do I get a copy of my records?
Email the practice manager. Records are released within one month at no charge, in line with
UK data protection rules. Ask for X-rays specifically if you want them, because they go as a
separate file.

## Do you have a complaints process?
Yes. Complaints go to the practice manager in writing, are acknowledged within three working
days, and are answered in full within twenty-one days. If you are not satisfied with the
outcome, the letter tells you how to take it to the Dental Complaints Service.

## Can I change my appointment by text?
Yes. Reply to the reminder text and it reaches the right site. That is the fastest route and
the one we would rather you used.

## Do you send reminders?
A confirmation email when you book and a text 48 hours before. You can opt out of either.

## Do you treat people who have not been to a dentist in years?
Routinely, and it is a much larger share of new patients than people assume. Nobody
comments on it, and the first appointment is an examination and a plan rather than
treatment, so there is no surprise on the day.

11-policies > Practice policies

# Practice policies


## Consent
Nothing is treated without consent, and for anything beyond a routine filling that consent
is written. The treatment plan is the basis for it, so you have the costs and the options in
front of you before you sign anything.

Consent can be withdrawn at any point, including mid-appointment. Raise a hand and the
clinician stops. That is a normal thing to do and every clinician here works that way.

## Data and records
Clinical records are kept for eleven years after the last appointment, or until a patient's
twenty-fifth birthday for children, whichever is longer. That is the standard UK retention
period.

Records are stored in a UK-hosted clinical system. They are not shared outside the practice
except with your consent, or where a clinician is legally obliged to.

You can ask for a copy of your records at any time, at no charge, and it is released within
one month.

Marketing emails go out only to patients who opted in, and the unsubscribe link works
immediately and permanently.

## Chaperones
A chaperone is available for any appointment on request, with no explanation needed. Ask at
the front desk when you book or on the day.

## Complaints
Complaints go to the practice manager in writing, by email or letter. They are acknowledged
within three working days and answered in full within twenty-one days.

If the answer does not resolve it, the response letter sets out how to escalate, which for
private treatment is the Dental Complaints Service and for a registration concern is the
General Dental Council.

We would rather hear about a problem early. Most complaints are about waiting time,
communication about cost, or a bite that was not adjusted, and all three are quick to fix if
somebody says so.

## Infection control
Instruments are sterilised on site in a validated autoclave with daily testing and a
logged audit trail. Single-use items are used where they exist. The infection control policy
is available at reception on request.

11-policies > Practice policies > Zero tolerance

## Zero tolerance
Abuse or threats towards staff end the appointment and the registration. This is not
negotiable and it applies at all three sites.

## Interpreters and accessibility
Between them the team speak English, Portuguese, Bengali, Polish and Cantonese, and the
front desk will arrange for a colleague who speaks your language to be present. A
professional interpreter can be arranged with a week's notice at no charge.

Docklands and Clapham are step-free. Shoreditch has a lift to the first floor. A hearing
loop is fitted at the Docklands front desk.

## Photography
Clinical photographs are taken for record keeping in most restorative and aesthetics cases,
and consent for that is separate and specific. Photographs are never used for marketing
without a further written consent that names that purpose.
